scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5093: After a user reboots their PC it cannot get an IP address. PCs
that were already up keep working, but newly connected devices on any internal
VLAN time out waiting for DHCP. The help desk reports this started after a
distribution-switch change and believes the DHCP relay (ip helper-address) on
the distribution switches is broken and no longer forwarding DHCPDISCOVER.
Please find and confirm the broken relay configuration on the DSWs.
scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-r1-dhcpd-down: the central ISC dhcpd on r1
is not running. r1 is the single DHCP server for every internal VLAN (A-PC,
A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi). The DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as
unicast to 10.0.0.76 (r1's loopback); the requests reach r1 but get no reply
because dhcpd is dead. Existing leases keep working until they expire; renewals
begin failing at lease-time/2.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a broken DHCP relay on the
distribution switches. The relay is FINE: the DSW ip-helper/relay config is
intact and is correctly unicasting to r1's loopback (10.0.0.76), which is still
routable. The fault is the central dhcpd daemon on r1, not the relay. A
decisive tell that the relay is not at fault: the symptom is identical across
EVERY VLAN behind EVERY distribution switch -- if a single DSW's relay were
broken, only the VLANs behind that one switch would fail; a single common DHCP
server (r1) failing is what explains the domain-wide DHCP outage. The
forwarding path to 10.0.0.76 is up (it is routable and reachable), so DISCOVERs
arrive at r1 and are simply dropped because no server is listening.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r1 (dhcpd not running).
The agent must localize to the dead server process on r1 and explicitly reject
the "broken relay" narrative -- the relay config is unchanged and the path to
the server is intact. An agent that goes hunting for (or fabricates) a broken
ip-helper/relay statement on the DSWs has followed the ticket's framing instead
of the evidence. Fix: restart dhcpd on r1
(`/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`).
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scoring_axes: must-identify-dhcpd-down: central dhcpd / DHCP server process not running on r1
bonus-rules-out-relay: notes the DSW relay/ip-helper config is intact and unicasting to a reachable 10.0.0.76, so the relay is not the cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected subsystem is the isc-dhcp-server daemon (dhcpd) on r1, which is the central DHCP server for all internal VLANs. When the lab was first inspected, dhcpd was not running but its PID file `/var/run/dhcpd.pid` was present — the hallmark of a process that started, wrote its PID, and was then forcefully terminated (SIGKILL or a crash), without the init script having a chance to remove the PID file. Because there was no DHCP server process listening on UDP 67, every DHCPDISCOVER relayed to r1's loopback (10.0.0.76) received no reply.

The relay layer is entirely healthy. Both distribution-switch primaries — dswa1 (Office A) and dswb1 (Office B) — are running `dhcrelay` with the correct VLAN sub-interfaces (`br0.10/20/40/99` and `br0.10/20/30/99` respectively) and the correct relay target (`10.0.0.76`). OSPF reachability from both relays to r1 is confirmed with 0% packet loss. dswa2 and dswb2 intentionally carry no relay daemon (per their startup scripts), and STP blocks their access-switch uplinks in any case, so all client broadcasts reach dswa1/dswb1 exclusively. The help desk hypothesis about broken `ip helper-address` configuration on the distribution switches is incorrect.

The mechanism explaining the user-visible symptom is straightforward: devices that were already online hold unexpired DHCP leases and continue to work without needing a new exchange; any device that reboots or connects fresh must complete a full DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK cycle, which requires a running server, and times out because dhcpd is dead.

Root cause: the isc-dhcp-server process on r1 was killed/crashed after lab startup, leaving a stale PID file and no DHCP server.

Corrective fix: restart the service on r1 with `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server start` (already confirmed working — dhcpd PID 302 is now running and the config passes `dhcpd -t` validation).

per_axis.axis: must-identify-dhcpd-down: central dhcpd / DHCP server process not running on r1
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states the isc-dhcp-server (dhcpd) on r1 was not running (stale PID file) and documents restarting it to restore service.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-relay: notes the DSW relay/ip-helper config is intact and unicasting to a reachable 10.0.0.76, so the relay is not the cause
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly verifies the DSW dhcrelay/ip-helper settings and reachability to 10.0.0.76 and rejects the relay-as-cause hypothesis, satisfying the axis.
The writeup instructs to start/restart the isc-dhcp-server on r1 (using /etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server start), which matches the expected remediation to restore dhcpd.

The log shows that r1 owns 10.0.0.76, r1 has no dhcpd running, and relays/DSWs can reach 10.0.0.76 — supporting the diagnosis that the central dhcpd on r1 is down rather than a broken relay, though some specific process-status outputs for the primaries and the final restart confirmation are only partially visible in the truncated log.
